summary: The note traces the introduction of the Christmas tree to Britain, which came about two centuries before the note was written. It credits Queen Charlotte, wife of George III, with holding a children's party featuring a Christmas tree in 1800. The custom stayed largely within the royal family at first, and Queen Victoria grew up with a tree in her room each Christmas. The note ends with a journal passage from Victoria's Christmas Eve 1832 entry, which is cut off before the quote itself.
one_line: Overview of how the Christmas tree custom reached Britain via Queen Charlotte in 1800 and the royal family, including Queen Victoria's childhood trees.
key_facts: The tradition of decorating homes with evergreens was long established before the custom of decorating an entire small tree reached Britain.
The custom of decorating an entire small tree was unknown in Britain until some two centuries ago.
Charlotte of Mecklenburg-Strelitz was the German-born wife of George III.
Charlotte introduced a Christmas tree at a party she gave for children in 1800.
The Christmas tree custom did not at first spread much beyond the royal family.
Queen Victoria as a child was familiar with the Christmas tree custom.
A tree was placed in Victoria's room every Christmas during her childhood.
Victoria wrote in her journal for Christmas Eve 1832, when she was 13 years old.
The note's excerpt of Victoria's 1832 journal entry ends with a colon before the quoted text, so the quote itself is not included.
